paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of deceived conversations across scenarios.
model_annotation: The figure is a horizontal grouped bar chart illustrating the distribution of conversations by whether participants were deceived (“Yes”, “Partially”, or “No”) across four scenarios. The category axis is the vertical (y) axis, which lists scenarios in top-to-bottom order: Academic Collaboration, Recruitment, Academic Funding, and Journalism; no explicit y-axis label is shown. The value axis is the horizontal (x) axis labeled “Number of Conversations” on a linear scale, with tick labels shown at regular intervals of 10 (0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60) and the plotted range extending to roughly 70. For each scenario, three separate bars are shown (grouped, not stacked): red represents “Yes,” yellow represents “Partially,” and green represents “No,” as indicated by the legend titled “Deceived” in the upper-right. Approximate bar lengths are: Academic Collaboration—Yes (red) ~36, Partially (yellow) ~27, No (green) ~7; Recruitment—Yes (red) ~38, Partially (yellow) ~24, No (green) ~6; Academic Funding—Yes (red) ~66, Partially (yellow) ~4, No (green) ~3; Journalism—Yes (red) ~15, Partially (yellow) ~47, No (green) ~6. The bars are arranged as grouped triplets per scenario with slight vertical offsets, and there is no visual indication that categories are sorted by bar magnitude or otherwise emphasized beyond the color coding and legend.
